subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core `gateway.peers` cross-gateway routing surface for session tools now, or keep this work behind the broader federation/security design tracked in the canonical issues?
rationale: The PR is more than a narrow tool fix: it adds config, remote routing, and a new trust boundary that can route agent tool calls across gateways.

options.title: Pause for federation design
options.body: Keep this PR open but do not repair or merge it until maintainers decide the peer trust, identity, auth, and operator-scope model.

options.title: Narrow to safe configured remote
options.body: Reject arbitrary `gatewayUrl` for sessions tools and only support a maintainer-approved configured remote path with explicit credentials and focused proof.

options.title: Adopt core peers with hardening
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require security review, protocol tests, idempotency fixes, token handling, conflict resolution, and live two-gateway proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Pause for federation design
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but do not repair or merge it until maintainers decide the peer trust, identity, auth, and operator-scope model.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history ties this owner signal to the gateway/session/protocol surfaces that would need the decision.
